taxonomic_note: Current Kew/POWO accepts Bothriochloa barbinodis at species rank and folds named varieties such as var. barbinodis into the species-level concept used by this learner.
look_here_first: Check the stem nodes before the seedhead. Cane bluestem has a conspicuous dense beard/ring of soft hairs around the node, often several millimeters long. Then confirm the fanlike silvery panicle: many primary branches spread nearly as long as the main inflorescence.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Williamson County — UT Plant Resources Center provides a detailed field-based treatment of Bothriochloa barbinodis. Val Verde County — the Amistad National Recreation Area vascular flora documents cane bluestem on rocky slopes and flats; USDA/Native Plants release data also include a Val Verde collection. Uvalde County — Texas Native Seeds/USDA collection data include a Bothriochloa barbinodis accession collected on Highway 55 south of the campground in Uvalde County.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: County PASS uses explicit county field/specimen/collection records. Broad Edwards Plateau or South Texas distribution is supporting context only.

best_field_traits: perennial warm-season cespitose bunchgrass, commonly 55–120 cm tall
culms erect or bent at base, usually unbranched above the base
nodes with a conspicuous dense ring of ascending soft hairs about 1.5–5 mm or longer
blades flat, long-tapered, commonly 2.5–6.5 mm wide
terminal panicle about 5–14 cm, dense and sometimes partly enclosed by upper sheath
primary branches numerous and relatively long, creating a broad fanlike mature head
silvery-white hairs conspicuous on the inflorescence
upper lemma awns long, bent and twisted, roughly 20–35 mm
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Bothriochloa torreyana: Silver bluestem has smooth/glabrous pale nodes and a contracted cottony panicle of many short rames; cane bluestem has the unmistakable hairy nodal beard and a broader fanlike head. Bothriochloa ischaemum: King Ranch bluestem has glabrous nodes and a loose 3–8-branched fingerlike/digitate seedhead rather than the bearded nodes and fanlike inflorescence of cane bluestem.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Silver bluestem has smooth/glabrous pale nodes and a contracted cottony panicle of many short rames; cane bluestem has the unmistakable hairy nodal beard and a broader fanlike head. King Ranch bluestem has glabrous nodes and a loose 3–8-branched fingerlike/digitate seedhead rather than the bearded nodes and fanlike inflorescence of cane bluestem.
